subject: Utility Trenching Standards and Preliminary Election Debate
overview: The Council established new expectations for utility companies regarding street restoration following conduit work and debated the merits of a proposed waiver for the preliminary municipal election. Significant discussion also focused on improving transparency for bond requests and addressing inconsistent parking enforcement.

items.title: Sisters Against Ovarian Cancer Awareness Campaign
items.summary: Approved a petition to hang teal bows throughout the city during September to raise awareness for ovarian cancer.

items.title: Special Permit Hearing: 3850 Mystic Valley Parkway
items.summary: Continued a public hearing for a special permit regarding extended hours at the Meadow Glen Mall to September 19 at the petitioner's request.

items.title: Comcast Conduit Petition: Washington Street
items.summary: Approved a petition to install underground conduits on Washington Street to service a Riverside Avenue bank.

items.title: AT&T Conduit Petition: Winchester Street
items.summary: Approved a large conduit relocation project for the Green Line Extension on the condition that the petitioner performs curb-to-curb street restoration and holds a pre-construction meeting with neighbors.

items.title: Comcast Conduit Petition: High Street
items.summary: Tabled a request for conduit work on High Street until September 19 to determine if the company will agree to the same curb-to-curb paving standards required of other recent petitioners.

items.title: National Grid Traffic Control Box
items.summary: Approved the installation of a traffic control box at the intersection of Wyman and Woburn streets to monitor an existing gas regulation station.

items.title: Preliminary Municipal Election Order
items.summary: Approved the order and polling locations for the preliminary municipal election scheduled for September 12, 2017.

items.title: Parking Enforcement Inconsistencies
items.summary: Placed on file a petition regarding inconsistent parking enforcement after hearing resident testimony about malfunctioning kiosks and questionable ticketing practices in residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Sign Denial Reversal: 400 High Street
items.summary: Referred a petition from the Evangelical Haitians Church regarding a sign denial to the subcommittee on signs to address concerns about internal illumination and size.

items.title: Stone and Skillet Records Request
items.summary: Approved a request for a comprehensive list of complaints, violations, and licenses associated with the business located at 186 Winthrop Street.

items.title: Bond Expenditure Transparency
items.summary: Approved a resolution requiring the administration to provide detailed, itemized breakdowns for all bond requests at least one week prior to a scheduled vote.

items.title: Gas Leak Ordinance and Soil Testing
items.summary: Scheduled a Committee of the Whole meeting to discuss a new ordinance for Level 3 gas leaks and approved a request for an update on soil borings behind Andrews School.

items.title: Wage Theft Ordinance Implementation
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a report on the implementation of the Wage Theft Ordinance and a list of all municipal vendors for the current and prior fiscal years.

items.title: Discussion on Waiving the Preliminary Election
items.summary: The Council discussed a previously withdrawn proposal to waive the preliminary election; several candidates spoke for and against the move, citing either potential cost savings or the importance of the democratic process.

items.title: Gas and Water Cost Resolutions
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state bills to prevent gas leak costs from being passed to consumers and amended it to request an administration study on 'unaccounted-for water' costs.

items.title: Water System Improvements Bond
items.summary: Passed the third and final reading of a bond totaling $2,075,000 for city-wide water system improvements.
